name: fokusflow
description: Read-only access to the applications, website monitoring status and alerts in your Fokusflow workspace.

interface.longDescription: Fokusflow keeps a founder's apps, services and website monitoring in one place. Connect it to check how your apps are doing without leaving the chat: list your applications and the services behind them, see the latest availability and response time for each monitored URL, and review open and recently closed alerts. Access is read-only; Fokusflow cannot change your workspace from here. Checks cover public website availability and response time, not server CPU, memory or disk. Requires a Fokusflow account.
defaultPrompt: Are any of my Fokusflow apps down right now?
Show my open Fokusflow alerts and when they started.
List my applications and the services each one uses.

positive.description: List the workspace's applications and their services
positive.prompt: What applications do I have in Fokusflow?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the workspace's one application, Demo Storefront, with its two services: Database (Supabase) and Storefront Web (Vercel).

positive.description: Check whether an application is up
positive.expected_behavior: Production (https://fokusflow.io) is healthy with HTTP 200 and staging (https://fokusflow.io/storefront) is down with HTTP 404, each with its response time and last check time.
Returns one open alert for the staging URL, with the time it started and the observed reason (HTTP 404).

positive.description: Recent failures and recovery, including closed alerts
positive.prompt: What broke recently and did it recover?
positive.expected_behavior: Reports the staging alert as still open and says nothing has recovered yet. Recently closed alerts may be empty.

positive.prompt: Give me a status summary of everything.
positive.expected_behavior: Summarises the application, its two monitors and the open alert, and names the failing staging monitor.

negative.description: Restarting a server is a write action. Fokusflow is read-only, so no tool should be called; the expected response explains that Fokusflow cannot restart servers.
Deleting a monitor is a write action. No tool should be called; the expected response explains that monitors are changed in the Fokusflow app.
Fokusflow does not collect CPU or memory metrics. The expected response gives no invented numbers and explains that checks cover availability and response time only.
negative.prompt: What's my server's CPU and memory usage?

review.commerce_description: Fokusflow for ChatGPT does not sell products or process payments.

publication.release_notes: Initial release: three read-only tools (list_applications, get_app_status, list_alerts) for checking applications, website availability and alerts in a Fokusflow workspace.
